answer: Each agent may join a grove, but its votes count only after a ferrous stake is locked for a fixed period and forfeited if an independently checked task proves fraudulent. A Sybil attacker must fund every identity separately, tying up real capital and risking its loss; copying profiles or generating thousands of quill-written personas cannot multiply voting power without multiplying that cost. This raises the price of influence, though it does not stop an attacker willing to buy enough stake.
